HISTORY AND CITIZENSHIP — MOCK EXAM #13
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: HISTORY AND CITIZENSHIP
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which statement about Colonial Administration in Africa is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Say Colonial Administration in Africa never happens in Kenya.
   B. Skip evidence when discussing Colonial Administration in Africa.
   C. Explain Colonial Administration in Africa with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   D. Treat Colonial Administration in Africa as rumours only.

   D. Treat Internal conflicts in Africa as rumours only.

6. A map key (legend) is used to: (1 mark)

   C. Treat Human Developments in Africa as rumours only.
   D. Skip evidence when discussing Human Developments in Africa.

8. A budget helps a family to: (1 mark)
   A. Ignore prices in shops
   B. Plan income and spending wisely
   C. Hide all money underground
   D. Avoid saving forever

9. Which statement about Political developments in independent Africa is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)

12. Which statement about Organisation of Kenyan Communities since 19th century is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Explain Organisation of Kenyan Communities since 19th century with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

13. Kenya’s capital city is: (1 mark)
   A. Kisumu
   B. Mombasa
   C. Nairobi
   D. Nakuru

14. Which statement about Civilisations in South and Central Africa is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Treat Civilisations in South and Central Africa as rumours only.

   A. Treat National Security as rumours only.

   D. Explain National Security with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

16. Which statement about French Revolutions is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Skip evidence when discussing French Revolutions.

   C. Treat French Revolutions as rumours only.
